title: Tenant probing and isolation profiles for burst mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity have reported intermittent latency spikes and throughput degradation when other tenants burst. Current hard-slicing and static quotas are effective but costly and inflexible for mixed workloads. We need a lower-cost, dynamic isolation layer that reduces noisy-neighbor effects while preserving burst allowance for legitimate short-term workloads.

Goal: Implement a tenant-probing and isolation-profiles system that: (1) uses lightweight probe windows to detect tenant burstiness and resource contention, (2) assigns a small set of isolation profiles per tenant (e.g., permissive, conservative, quarantined) based on risk and historical patterns, and (3) integrates with autoscaler and eviction scoring to gracefully throttle or evict low-priority work when necessary. The solution must be observable, reversible (soft-fallbacks), and require minimal config from customers by default.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline: end-to-end smoke test demonstrates that a noisy synthetic tenant no longer increases 95th percentile latency of neighbor tenants by >10% under the same workload mix
Isolation profiles: each tenant can be placed into one of three profiles and changes are logged and visible in Console
Probing: probe windows run at sub-minute cadence and generate metrics (probe_success, probe_latency, probe_retries) that feed autoscaler decisions
Autoscaler integration: when a tenant is moved to 'conservative', autoscaler enforces burst caps and triggers fallback routes instead of immediate hard evictions
Eviction scoring: eviction decisions use harmonized score including probe-derived contention, recent SLO violations, and tenant priority
Safety: default behavior for new tenants is 'permissive', and any isolation action can be rolled back automatically within 5 minutes if latency impact increases
Observability: dashboards and alerting for probe anomalies, profile transitions, and top-10 tenants by isolation score are shipped
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight admission/probing controller in the request routing layer that periodically issues short synthetic requests (probes) under controlled resources to estimate a tenant's burst propensity and tail latency contribution. Map probe signals + historical telemetry (95th/99th latency, token rate variance) to one of three isolation profiles with configurable thresholds. Hook the profile into the runtime token-bucket admission filter and the autoscaler policy: permissive profiles get higher burst tokens, conservative profiles get reduced burst windows and priority-based queueing, quarantined profiles are rate-limited and routed to a fallback model variant. Eviction scoring will add a 'contention_penalty' derived from probe failure rate, which increases preemption weight for low-priority jobs. All transitions are recorded in the audit log and surfaced in Console with the reason and time window.
implementation_plan: WIP: design probe payloads and frequency with Research (safe minimal tokens)
Build: admission/probing controller service (k8s) with API for profile assignments
Runtime: extend token-bucket admission filter to accept profile overrides and apply dynamic burst windows
Autoscaler: add profile-aware scaling rules and a fast rollback trigger when latency regresses
Eviction: update eviction scorer to include 'contention_penalty' and weight tuning
Observability: Grafana dashboard (probe metrics, profile transitions), Console surface for per-tenant profile and recent probe history
Docs & Runbook: public-facing FAQ + internal runbook for incidents and manual overrides

notes: Trade-offs considered: full hard-slicing avoids noisy neighbors entirely but increases cost and reduces utilization. Probing + profiles reduces cost but adds complexity and probabilistic behavior.
Privacy: probe payloads are synthetic, deterministic seeds and do not contain customer data. Confirmed with Security that no additional data residency controls are required.
Signal hygiene: to avoid probe amplification we will sample tenants for probing and progressively expand sampling if instability observed.

Fallback paths: we prefer routing to smaller, quantized model variants before evicting requests to keep customer-facing errors low. This requires expanded model-variant catalog for Dedicated customers.
